problems: The new LNCaP peak evidence strengthens occupancy support for FOXA1, HOXB13, and XBP1, but none of the cited ChIP-seq evidence establishes allele-specific occupancy.

For all five chains, greater C-than-T binding is predicted in vitro rather than demonstrated in cells; the reported C prostate-cancer effect allele is directionally consistent with that prediction, but no gene-expression or disease mechanism direction is established.

RFX6 is a plausible candidate based on intragenic location and prostate-cancer L2G scores, but no supplied evidence directly connects EH38E2496909 to RFX6. The listed element links instead include VGLL2 contacts in other biosamples and an adipose FAM162B eQTL.

The cCRE's enhancer activity in the matched LNCaP context is unknown; none of the 170 SCREEN core biosamples matches the supplied context. No single TF chain is established as best supported by these data.

games.reason: The shared element, target-gene, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains. Both TFs are expressed in LNCaP and have nearby ChIP-seq summits, and the family-screen evidence supports the same in-vitro C-over-T binding direction for both. FOXA1 is better supported because its summit is closer to the variant (2 bp versus 27 bp) and ReMap independently reports multiple LNCaP FOXA1 peaks containing the variant, with the nearest summit 2 bp away.

FOXA1 has stronger variant-proximal occupancy evidence: it is highly expressed in LNCaP and has a ChIP-seq summit 2 bp from the variant (E14), with ReMap reporting multiple variant-overlapping FOXA1 peaks in LNCaP, including one with a summit 2 bp away (E25). NKX3-1 is also expressed and has a nearby LNCaP summit, but it is 27 bp from the variant (E13). The shared family-screen evidence indicates greater in-vitro binding to C than T, but the more direct ChIP evidence favors FOXA1 (E12).
